The chain of components that led to the error, shown to help find the cause.

sections.name: File setup, Props, State
sections.title: Imports and the inputs
sections.what: Brings in the React error types, the load-failure check, and defines the inputs (the protected page and the home address) and the state that holds an error.
sections.why: Likely reason: the boundary needs a place to keep the error it caught and a link home to offer.

sections.name: PageErrorBoundary
sections.title: Catching errors and showing the panel
sections.what: Catches an error from the page inside, logs it to the console, and shows an alert panel. The panel explains either a failed download or an unexpected error, and offers reloading or returning to the tools page.
sections.why: Likely reason: a readable message with a way out is easier for users than a blank screen.
sections.watch_out: Reloading can lose unsaved edits, and the panel warns about this, so nothing is saved automatically when an error happens.

summary: A safety net around each page that catches unexpected crashes and shows a plain message with reload and return options, instead of a blank screen.
purpose: Stops one broken page from taking down the whole app and tells the user what to do next.
why: Likely reason: an uncaught error in React would otherwise leave an empty screen. The separate message for failed file downloads is visible in the code.
how: 1. Watches for an error from the page inside it. 2. Records the error and logs it to the browser console with the component stack. 3. Shows an alert panel whose message depends on whether files failed to load. 4. Offers Reload page and Return to tools.
inputs: The page to protect (its children), the address of the home page, and any error the page throws.
outputs: Either the page itself or the error panel. A console log entry for each error.
risks: Reloading can discard unsaved edits, which the panel warns about. Once an error is recorded, the panel stays until the page reloads.
debug: Check the browser console for the logged message and component stack. The load-failure wording depends on the isModuleLoadError check in lazyPage.
